_comment: Two rules are disabled here, each for a measured, repo-specific reason; the shipped defaults stay neutral and this is the consuming repo's own decision, which is what the config layer is for. (1) rule-em-dash: this marketplace's house style uses em dashes deliberately, measured 34,999 matching lines across 1229 tracked markdown files (2026-08-19), which is a style choice, not a defect backlog. Disabling beats enumerating em_dash_allowed_paths, which would need near-total path coverage to be useful. (2) rule-curly-artifacts: punctuation glyphs were already ruled out of scope by the repo owner, twice in writing, and the rule's yield is almost entirely the material those rulings protect. Measured 2026-08-20 over 1214 tracked markdown files: 72 findings, of which 39 are quoted Pat Pattison book text, 32 are a verbatim pasted external Codex review, and exactly 1 was genuine paste residue (a stray curly apostrophe in plugins/disk-hygiene/README.md, fixed rather than suppressed in the same change as this entry). The rulings: plugins/songwriting/context/pat-pattison/research/book-references.md ('Do not sweep, measure, audit, or open work items on punctuation glyphs' - a session was spent on exactly that before the owner ruled it out of scope; it also notes the four books disagree with each other, so there is no fidelity axis to restore toward) and the songwriting CHANGELOG entry 'PUNCTUATION GLYPHS ARE NOT A FIDELITY AXIS - DO NOT SWEEP FOR THEM', which records a prior session normalizing 470 lines before the ruling landed. A per-path exemption would be the narrower instrument, but the config layer supports that only for rule-em-dash today; generalizing it is left to its own change. Revisit if a corpus of genuine LLM paste residue ever lands here.
